blocks.intro: When most of a town's plumbing is the same age, the emergencies follow a pattern.

items.body: Roots in old clay can stop a line overnight.
Galvanized and cast iron can fail without warning.
In May 2020, 7.35 inches of rain fell on Skokie in five days.

blocks.h2: What to Do on a Storm Night
blocks.body: If rain is heavy and water starts rising at the floor drain, stop using water in the house so you're not adding to it. Check that the sump pump is running and has power. Move valuables off the basement floor. If sewage is coming up, keep everyone out of the water. Then call us. We'll clear the line and, once the storm passes, talk about protection.

blocks.h2: The Emergencies Skokie Homeowners Call About Most
blocks.body: Most of our urgent Skokie calls are sewer backups through the basement floor drain, sump and ejector pumps that stop during storms, frozen pipes on outside walls and water heaters that leak without warning. Each has a quick first step while we're on the way: stop using water, check the pump's power or shut off the main.

blocks.h2: Emergency Plumbing Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.answer: Yes. Our phone line is open 24/7, including weekends and holidays.

items.q: What should I do until you get here?
items.preview: Shut off the water and stay safe.
items.answer: For a leak, close the main valve. For a backup, stop using water. Stay out of water near outlets.

items.q: Where's the main water shutoff in a Skokie home?
items.preview: Usually in the basement at the front wall.
items.answer: In most homes, it's in the basement where the water line comes in from the street, near the meter.

items.q: Will I know the price before you start?
items.answer: Yes. You'll get a flat-rate price before any work begins.

items.q: How quickly can you get to me?
items.answer: Arrival times depend on the day and the weather, but we work to get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.q: Should I call during a storm or wait?
items.answer: Call if water is rising or the sump pump has stopped.

items.q: Can you help if my overhead sewer pump stops?
items.answer: Yes. Stop using basement fixtures and call us.
